references.text: Prohibition against doing injustice in judgment, and command to judge righteously without regard to a person's status—whether the lowly or the powerful.
Warning against showing favoritism to the poor in his lawsuit, emphasizing impartiality in judgment.
Moses' father-in-law Jethro's advice on appointing judges, and that difficult cases should be brought to Moses—a parallel to the system described here.
Prohibition against perverting justice, showing partiality, or accepting bribes in judgment.
Fear of man sets a trap, but whoever trusts in the Lord is safe—a parallel to the command not to fear any person.
Jehoshaphat exhorts the judges that they judge for the Lord, not for men, and that they must not show partiality or accept bribes.
Warning against making distinctions among people based on outward circumstances, reflecting the same principle of impartiality.
Peter's recognition that God shows no favoritism but accepts anyone who fears him—God's impartiality as a model.
God shows no favoritism; his judgment is impartial, just as judges should be.
God judges among the gods and rebukes those who judge unjustly and take the side of the wicked.
